problem.text: The stated goal is equal K/V projection bitrates; two existing allocation candidates increased V alone.

reasoning.text: The change raises K's increment to match V in two Q/K/V/O patterns, replacing [0,0,1,0] and [0,0,2,0] with [0,1,1,0] and [0,2,2,0]. It changes the candidate search space rather than enforcing equality after selection.

impact.text: For those candidates, matching K to V costs additional bits proportional to K's weight count. This can change the selected allocation and the surplus returned to the caller; MLP-only allocation is unaffected.

source_notes.text: The root conversion entry describes allocation as a fixed size-based heuristic rather than a calibration-error search, and records an exact-budget selection boundary.

limitations: No model conversion, GPU execution, quality evaluation or performance measurement was performed. Checks executed an extracted allocator with synthetic projection objects and the two substitutions applied in memory.

chapters.title: Pair K/V increments in the allocation heuristic

claims.text: allocate_transformer orders attention projections as Q/K/V/O. Its pattern entries are integer bitrate increments above floor(effective budget per weight), with a minimum base of one and a per-projection cap of eight. Attention and MLP candidates are combined, costed using projection weight counts, and sorted for budget selection.

Both direct callers, TransformerBlock.allocate_q and ParallelDecoderBlock.allocate_q, pass their attention projections in that order and return the strategy and surplus unchanged. They bypass allocation only when both attention and MLP are absent.

With four 128-weight attention projections, target 3 and incoming surplus 383, the extracted parent allocator returned Q/K/V/O = 3/3/5/3; applying the patch returned 3/4/4/3. Both returned surplus 128: this example redistributes the same bit cost from V to K.

The patch leaves both the unequal [0,1,2,1] candidate and the inherited exact-cost bisect boundary intact. Thus the change does not establish universal K/V equality or correct the previously documented budget boundary.

findings.description: A retained candidate can still allocate different K and V bitrates, contrary to the commit's stated goal.
findings.trigger: Attention-only allocation with Q/K/V/O weight counts 256/128/128/256, target 3 and incoming surplus 640.
findings.expected_behavior: K and V receive equal bitrates if the stated goal is universal.
findings.actual_behavior: The patched allocator selects 3/4/5/4 and returns surplus 1.

verification.description: Executed the extracted parent function with the two task substitutions and synthetic objects providing keys and weight counts.
verification.limits: Not a complete conversion. Both inspected block callers expose this allocator; occurrence of these budgets in real models was not measured.

findings.description: The inherited exact-cost candidate exclusion remains unchanged.
findings.trigger: Four 128-weight attention projections, target 3 and incoming surplus 255 yield budget 1792, exactly matching the patched 3/4/4/3 candidate.
findings.expected_behavior: Select the largest candidate within budget, including an exact match.
findings.actual_behavior: bisect_right searches with (budget,), which sorts before equal-cost two-element tuples; allocation instead returns 3/3/3/3 with surplus 256.

verification.description: Executed the extracted, patched allocator on the exact-budget example.
verification.limits: Synthetic projection objects only. The condition applies through either inspected block caller when its budget matches a candidate cost.

annotation.summary: Pairs K/V increments in two allocation candidates, but a remaining unequal candidate prevents a universal equality guarantee.
